entries.title: grow arrays in place; Copy a push loop over an array range in one memcpy
entries.body:
An array built by push no longer costs the sum of every size it passed
through. nish_array_grow grows the block where it is: by a bump when the
data is the arena's last block, or by a realloc of the exact chunk a block
over 64 KB fills; anything else takes the copy. NISH_REUSE_CAP keeps a chunk
past 64 KB that is reused from its start one word short, so a scope's mark is
never under a reallocated chunk; a smaller chunk stays whole, so a recycled
async task region still fits its next task. The --debug-arena build always
copies, because its chunks are never malloc'd.

A for loop whose body is one dst.push(src[P + j]) now copies the range in
one guarded memcpy. Whatever a guard refuses runs the unchanged loop, so an
out-of-range index still panics where it did.

bench/goose/ ports five Goose benchmarks and records the results. The
runtime's .text budgets move: core 1,805 -> 2,098 bytes, threads
2,010 -> 2,300.
metrics: peak RSS on Goose's large size, records 392 -> 179 MB, strlist 358 -> 162 MB, words 804 -> 411 MB (best of three, noise under 1%); words at 16M words about 11% faster (run-to-run noise about 4%); instructions Queens +0.14%, Bounce -0.4%
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: give every page a canonical link, its own titles and a theme-color
entries.body: Each page route in scalar.config.json now carries a generated head: a title with the site name, a bare og:title and a canonical link. scripts/route-head.mjs writes them and its --check catches drift. page.js writes theme-color from the current light or dark background and takes the JSON-LD headline from og:title. Scalar has no title template and loads head scripts only by URL, so JSON-LD stays client-side; docs/README.md records why.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: give net_relay_f64 its own scratch directory
entries.body:
net_relay and net_relay_f64 run the same checks, and setup.ts wrote the PEM pair its renewal checks watch to the fixed paths build/net_relay/chain.pem and key.pem. The link pool runs both programs at once, so each overwrote the files the other was about to load. The mtime-only RelayWatch read the other's writes as a renewal. That is the intermittent PEM/renewal failure CI saw in runs 43941217022 and 44156052604.

relayChecks and setupChecks now take the scratch directory as a required parameter, and each entry names its own directory. No retry, no skip and no serialisation. The two built apps run side by side failed in 20 of 20 iterations before the change and in 0 of 20 after.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: hold the crypto specs to vector 0.4.0's rows instead of transcribed properties
entries.body:
Four specs now say with vector rows what they could only say with a property
or an Untested paragraph before 0.4.0, so fidelity holds every printed byte to
its RFC.

- RFC 7748 §6.1 is four rows under the RFC's own labels ("Alice's private key,
  a", "Their shared secret, K"), replacing P-DH-VECTOR, whose bytes nothing
  checked against the RFC.
- RFC 4231 test case 5 is three rows with a `Truncate: … to 128 bits`
  paragraph each, replacing P-TRUNC-256, -384 and -512.
- RFC 8439's quarter-round vectors (§2.1.1, §2.2.1) are rows over the `u32[]`
  state, so chacha20QuarterRound is tested rather than out of scope; the A.1,
  A.2 and A.4 rows cite their own Test Vector.
- RFC 8032 §7.1's five signatures each get an ed25519Verify row whose result
  is cited to §5.1.7 and derived by P-ROUNDTRIP, which now draws messages up
  to 1,023 bytes so TEST 1024's is in range.

contracts/README.md names these forms and points at .vector-version instead
of naming a vector version. Nothing under std/, src/ or runtime/ changes.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: move to vector 0.5.0
entries.body:
vector 0.5.0 replays every counterexample exactly, refuses a property that
restates the row it derives, and names a refusal's own markdown line. Every
contract and generated test is byte-identical under it, so only the pin
moves.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: fail the fnref peak checks only on growth
entries.body: The section 4.4 "no reference call leaks" checks compared two peak resident sets with an absolute bound, so a second peak lower than the first by one arena chunk failed. A leak only raises the second peak, so the checks now bound growth only: the second peak may not exceed the first by 128 KB.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: free an idle ring slot's receive queue
entries.body:
A ring slot's receive queue was allocated at 4 KiB on first receive and
freed only when the connection closed, so every idle keep-alive slot held
it. nr_read now frees the queue once it drains it, and the queue starts at
1,024 bytes, inside glibc's tcache. A slot reused at accept never carries a
queue, because every path that frees a slot runs after nr_close's free.

Recorded as NURING-38 in docs/security/net-uring.md, with a net_ring check
that holds idle ring connections and bounds the server's memory per idle
connection; the base runtime fails it.

Measured: bench/handler-ring at 96,000 connections, PSS 141.4-141.7 MB on the ring against S4's 518 MB (docs/BENCHMARKS.md)
Refs: docs/security/net-uring.md, docs/BENCHMARKS.md
Tests: tests/link/net_ring_idle
Part of #1708
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: echo ECN counts in the QUIC server's ACKs
entries.body:
The server now counts the ECN codepoint each new packet arrived with, per packet-number space (ECT(0), ECT(1), CE), and once any count is above zero sends its ACKs as ACK_ECN (RFC 9000 §13.4.1). A duplicate counts nothing; each coalesced packet counts once. Http3Server passes the codepoint udpRecvFrom reports to the connection through QuicConnection.arrivalEcn.

Refs: docs/security/quic.md#quic-10
Tests: tests/link/net_quic_ecn

Fixes #759
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: measure Nish's crypto against OpenSSL, Go, Rust and Node, portable and with assembly
entries.body:
node bench/run.mjs --only crypto writes a "Crypto against other languages" section into docs/BENCHMARKS.md. Every kernel runs as Nish (with its runtime kernels and portable, with NISH_AES, NISH_CHACHA20 and NISH_SHA256 set to soft), OpenSSL (and OPENSSL_ia32cap-masked), Go (and purego), Rust (and soft) and Node. Checksums agree across all nine, the kernels join the instruction-count gate and --validate, and docs/crypto-performance.md analyses every cell more than 1.5x behind portable code.

Measured: AES-128-GCM seal at 1350 B: 93.7 MB/s portable and 708 MB/s on the kernel, against 130 (Rust soft) and 822 MB/s (OpenSSL)
Refs: docs/BENCHMARKS.md#crypto-against-other-languages, docs/crypto-performance.md
Fixes #475
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: give netShutdown and netMss a slot path
entries.body:
netShutdown on a NET_LISTEN_RING slot used to reach shutdown(2) with the
slot handle and answer -9, so Http1Server's lingering close on a ring
listener fell back to an immediate close and could reset a client that was
still sending. A slot's shutdown now goes through the ring as
IORING_OP_SHUTDOWN, queued behind the slot's pending sends so the FIN
follows the bytes already written, and a close waits for a shutdown in
flight. A closed or stale handle still answers -9.

SHUTDOWN joins the restricted rings' allowed ops. The ring layer only ever
submits it on a fixed file of the ring's own table, as it does SEND; the
restriction whitelists SQE flags but does not require FIXED_FILE, which is
recorded as NURING-39. A kernel without the op keeps the listener on epoll.

netMss on a slot answers -1, as it did, now explicitly and documented: the
MSS of a direct descriptor cannot be read without IORING_OP_URING_CMD, which
would widen the restriction set. The guide and nish.d.ts say so, where the
guide had said -9.

runtime-net.c's .text budget rises from 11,008 to 11,264 bytes, measured at
11,190.

Tests: tests/link/net_ring_linger, tests/runtime/uring-test.c (shutclose)
Refs: docs/security/net-uring.md, docs/guide/using-nish/networking.md
Part of #1708
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: accept a WebSocket without leaving bytes in the arena
entries.body:
Http1Connection.acceptWebSocket built the Sec-WebSocket-Accept value as a fresh string on every upgrade, so a long-lived server's arena grew by the key, its SHA-1 and its base64 on each accepted connection. The connection now owns a WsAcceptKey (a Sha1 state and a 28-byte buffer) made on the first upgrade and reused after it; Sha1.digestInto and base64StdPadEncodeInto write into it, and websocketWriteUpgradeResponse sends the response from those bytes. This closes H1-3, the way HpackDecoder closed H2-1.

Refs: docs/security/http1-codec.md#h1-3
Tests: tests/link/net_http1_server (acceptsFlat), tests/link/net_websocket
Fixes #447
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: carve the arena from a reserved range when a program has a compact class
metrics: bench/goose/tree.ts at depth 24, 21 rounds, range runtime against stock: +2.5% wall, within the median per-round ptr vs ptr-copy band (3.5%) and the widest (16.8%); peak RSS within 0.2 MB. Runtime .text at -Oz: default rows unchanged (2,098 / 2,300 B); range build 2,695 / 2,917 B.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: record the ring's p99 as a queue on one core, and measure 300,000 connections
entries.body:
One ring process's p99 trailed five SO_REUSEPORT epoll processes in an
external SQLite entry (65 against 20 ms at 90,000 keep-alive connections).
bench/handler-ring now measures it. loadgen records per-request latency
with a configurable keep-alive think time and reports p50, p99 and p99.9
over a steady window. The window excludes the connect burst and counts
failed sends, closed connections and requests left unanswered.

At matched load on one core the ring's p99 was the lower one in every round
(96,000 connections, 4 s think: ring 1.55 to 1.78 ms against epoll from
2.27 ms). One epoll process alone tails as well, worse than the ring at
45,000 a second. bench/handler-ring/trace.patch, run by trace.sh, counts
passes, pumps, waits and the ready list. It shows no pass long enough to
explain the tail and a ready list that queues behind one core. So the stage
records the cause, a queue on one core, rather than changing the runtime.

At 300,000 connections one ring process held 436 MB PSS at 23.7 µs a
request, with a p99 of 0.90 ms.

Refs: docs/BENCHMARKS.md, docs/wp63-iouring-net.md
Part of #1708
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: run each duplicated check once per push
entries.body: Four checks ran twice on every push. The test job's sanitizers section ran runtime_sanitize and the fuzz replays that fuzz-smoke also runs; it now reports them as DELEGATED under --delegate-sanitizers (honoured only under GitHub Actions), and a tests/run.js guard fails if fuzz-smoke stops running them unconditionally. A local npm test still runs both. The runner job, which pushed the golden corpus through the harness written in Nish and made only assertions the test shards also make, now runs on the release: the Release PR and the v* tag run release.yml makes of ci.yml. A guard holds that gate, and the nishRunner section's pop run still proves the harness on every push. npm run check moves from all eight test shards to the lint job, and the shard-2 SHA-256 throughput step, which printed figures and asserted nothing the simd section does not, is removed.
metrics: 176.9 -> 125.5 runner-minutes for one push (main run 44224030613 against PR run 44237099813, one run each); test x8 90.7 -> 77.2, runner x3 36.4 -> 0
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: test a counted loop's x + i for overflow once, before the loop
entries.body:
A checked `x + i` inside a counted `for` loop, where `x` does not change in the loop and `i` steps by one between known bounds, now tests both ends of the range once in the loop's preheader. When neither end can overflow, the loop body uses `add nsw`. Otherwise it runs the unchanged checked addition, so an addition that really overflows still panics at the same operation with the same message. The guard applies only to a local or constant `x` that the loop body never writes, and it is never shared across functions or async resume points.

A callgrind profile of bench/goose/words.ts put 31.9% of instructions on `same()`, string equality on the map's probe path, which paid two `llvm.sadd.with.overflow` branches per byte. The FNV-1a `hash()` took 13.25%, so `same()` was the larger cost and is the one fixed here. bench/goose/README.md records the profile, the fix, and `hash()` as the next step.
metrics: words at 16M words, best of 10 alternating runs: 3548 ms (range 3548 to 4053) before, 3110 ms (3110 to 3423) after. The ranges do not overlap: 12% faster. Under callgrind, total instructions fell from 1,603.5M to 1,368.3M, and `same()` fell from 512.0M to 239.4M. The words binary grows by 112 bytes.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: rewrite the reject_* golden cases to arrow declarations
entries.body:
The reject_* golden cases now declare their functions as `const NAME = (...) => {...}`, the declaration form WP22 settled on. The rewrite is scripts/arrowify.mjs with block bodies only, so no line moves and every pinned diagnostic keeps its code, message and position.

Cases where the `function` keyword is the thing under test keep it: reject_fn_nested, reject_fn_anonymous, reject_ffi_body, reject_generator, reject_export_default and reject_export_c_symbol_function, along with every `declare function`, generator and `async function`.

Part of #1722 (WP22 stage C, the test corpus).
entries.author: Redis Stasa

entries.title: correct the ring slot's netShutdown and netMss answers and the io_uring counts
entries.body:
docs/LANGUAGE.md still said netShutdown and netMss answer -9 on a ring slot.
Since NURING-39, netShutdown shuts a slot down through the ring behind its
queued sends, a later netWrite answers -32 after a write shut, and netMss
answers -1. The reference page is regenerated from it.

The security index's io_uring row now counts NURING-38 as fixed: twenty fixed,
two open, seventeen decided. docs/BENCHMARKS.md says the earlier loadgen
closed its window after take()'s sample reads, not after its last /proc
reads, and marks the share of a request's CPU that a pumped completion
carries as an inference.

Part of #1728
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: link the compiler under test once per compiler input
entries.body:
fuzz-smoke and postgres-live built their compiler with `npm run build`, which links stage1 and then stage2 from it. They now take the test job's stage1 through the compiler-cache action, under the same key and without saving. nish-cmp elision's candidate, the same `--link` made with its row's seed, now comes through the cache too. On a cache hit each of these jobs copies the binary instead of linking it. stage2 is still built and exercised on every push by `bootstrap (x86_64-linux)`, which asserts IR(stage1) == IR(stage2).

The roughly 80 s per test shard seen in run 44241824047 was a legitimate miss: that push to main changed src/, so it made a new key. On a hit the cache already restores in seconds, so the test job needed no change. Also fixes two stale descriptions from #1724: the ci.yml header still listed the typecheck under `test`, and docs/wp10-ci.md gave the wrong simd step count.
metrics: one PR run (44253614689) against the 39-run baseline medians: fuzz-smoke 6.3 -> 4.5 min, postgres-live 3.6 -> 1.8, nish-cmp elision x86_64 5.1 -> 3.5, aarch64 3.9 -> 3.6; test shard summaries identical to main's 44252691648 (77935 passed, 0 failed, 17 skipped)
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: rewrite the link programs and wording cases to arrow declarations
entries.body:
Every module under tests/link and tests/wordings now declares its functions as `const NAME = (...) => {...}`, the declaration form WP22 settled on. The rewrite uses scripts/arrowify.mjs with block bodies only, so no line moves and every pinned wording is unchanged. The diagnostics reference pages that quote the wording cases are regenerated with scripts/gen-reference.mjs.

The tests/wordings/host modules keep `export function`. They are host modules, page TypeScript that src/host-module.ts reads without a parser, and that reader keeps only `export function` signatures.

Part of #1722 (WP22 stage C, the test corpus).
entries.author: Redis Stasa

entries.title: rewrite the differential corpus and the remaining fixtures to arrow declarations
entries.body:
The differential corpus and the small fixture directories now declare their functions as `const NAME = (...) => {...}`. That covers tests/fix, tests/parser, tests/layout, tests/emit-ts, tests/host-import, tests/module-storage and tests/page. The rewrite is scripts/arrowify.mjs with block bodies only.

The frozen differential rewrites are keyed on a hash of their sources, and nothing can re-freeze one since stage0 was retired. So `tests/differential/goldens.js` gains `--rekey-arrowified --rev <ref>`, which moves a stale record's key only when two checks pass:
- every module's source at <ref> hashes to the frozen key;
- arrowify's own block-bodied rewrite of that source gives the working-tree bytes exactly.

Anything else stays stale, is named, and exits non-zero. All 157 frozen programs stay frozen.

Kept as `function`, because the declaration form is what they test or what their reader needs: host modules (src/host-module.ts reads only `export function` signatures), parser fixtures about `function` parsing, and three `nish --fix` fixtures whose subject is the declaration kind.

Part of #1722 (WP22 stage C, the test corpus).
entries.author: Redis Stasa

entries.title: split the test runner's lines sixteen positions at a time with nish:simd, and add simd variants checked against scalar
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: raise strbuild and map-proto-ordered-fp32 instruction baselines
entries.body:
Both counts rose in runtime commits whose CI passed: strbuild at 2f4f8e30 (the per-lane arena's carved-bit check) and map-proto-ordered-fp32 at 6074bbec (nish_str_from_i32 no longer inlined). bench/instructions.json mixes counts from the cloud container and from CI's runner, so the container's --check failed where CI's did not. Both baselines now take the container's counts. The instructions section prints its count table on a pass too, and bench/README.md records which environment each count comes from. bench/goose/README.md adds a before row for words, before/after geomeans with their noise band, and a 16M callgrind split of hash() and same().

Fixes #1727

entries.title: pin benchmark-table provenance and stale-pointer greps in CLAUDE.md
entries.body:
Two conventions the wp63-ring-gaps run kept rediscovering. Every
BENCHMARKS.md table names the commit whose bench code produced it,
claims only the fields that version prints, and quotes a per-second
maximum as a maximum. A builtin whose answer changes is grepped across
LANGUAGE.md, the guide and nish.d.ts, and a security record's count change
moves its docs/security/README.md row.

entries.title: rewrite the positive golden cases to arrow declarations
entries.body:
Every non-reject tests/cases program now declares its functions as `const NAME = (...) => {...}`, the declaration form WP22 settled on. That is 630 rewrites in 255 files.

The rewrite is scripts/arrowify.mjs with block bodies only, so no line moves and every .ll golden is byte-identical. Cases where `function` is the subject (`declare function`, `async function`, the stage-B parity case) are left alone.

entries.author: Redis Stasa

entries.title: report which classes the compact-class rule picks, with --explain-layout
entries.body:
`nish --explain-layout` prints, for every class in a program, whether WP48's compact-class rule (docs/wp48-ref32-classes.md §3.1) would pick it. For each class it gives the first of the five tests that refuses it and the size before and after narrowing. It changes no byte of the IR, and no program's layout moves. The rule lives in its own module, src/compact-rule.ts, and codegen does not call it yet. Stage 3 switches it on once stage 2's emitter lands, and the report can already survey the compiler and the corpus.

Test 1 passes only for a closed native build: `--link` or `nish run`. A bare `-o` build is refused because a host may link the IR. So are wasm32, `--emit-ts`, the C and N-API sidecars, and a module that declares a C function. Test 4 finds recursion in the direct-call graph of the parsed bodies, generic functions and methods included. A name that a parameter or local shadows is not counted as an edge. The report confirms the design's three figures: `TNode` 24 → 12 bytes in bench/goose/tree.ts, `TNode` 16 → 8 in bench/goose/bintrees.ts, and the node in bench/wp48-refs/sibling.ts 32 → 20.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: refuse a new function definition in the test corpus
entries.body: Biome reads src/, std/ and examples/, not tests/, so nothing kept the test corpus spelled as arrows. A new tests/run.js check, arrow-corpus, fails on any tests/**/*.ts file holding a top-level definition scripts/arrowify.mjs would rewrite unless tests/function-spelling-allowlist.txt lists it with a reason, and on a listed file that no longer holds one, so the list only shrinks. The inline Nish the JS harnesses write out, and the fuzz generator's programs, are now const arrows. WP22 stage C is done (4 of 5).
entries.author: Redis Stasa

entries.title: let knip know prlimit is a system tool
entries.body: tests/run.js is about to run the checks that expect a SIGSEGV under util-linux's prlimit, so the kernel writes no core of the debug arena's 1 TiB reservation (#1739). knip reports any binary a script spawns that no package provides, so prlimit joins the system tools in ignoreBinaries beside clang, gdb and unshare. Until #1739 lands, knip reports the entry as a configuration hint, which does not fail it.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: deal the test shards by today's costs
entries.body:
Shard 5 was the slowest test shard in 40 of 48 runs, at a median of 14.8 min against 9.4 for the typical shard, and it set PR feedback time. The debug-arena and compact-class range checks that expect a SIGSEGV made the runner dump a core of the whole 1 TiB reservation, at 81 to 303 s each, and the cost table dealt runtimeChecks as 54 s when it took about 524 s. Those checks now run under util-linux's `prlimit --core=1:1`; a limit of 1 is the one the kernel reads as "no core" for a piped core_pattern too. Without prlimit on the path they run as before, and the suite prints a NOTE saying so. Each check still asserts the same signal and output.

tests/shard-costs.json could not be refit before this: scripts/shard-costs.mjs failed on three sections that had no recognizer (h1Between, unboundedPass, breakWeb). The script now knows their first checks. It also takes `--drop <regex>`, which measures runs logged before a fix as though the matching checks took no time. The table is refit from five green post-#1721 main runs with `--drop '^debug arena.*dies of SIGSEGV'`. The runner job's `--check-runner` slices were checked locally against the new table.
metrics: PR run 44273081341 against main run 44270405010 (one run each). Wall time 17m41s -> 11m44s. Slowest/median shard 1.61 -> 1.19. Shard 5 Test step 935 -> 438 s. Runner-minutes 133.4 -> 119.0. The eight shards sum to 78047 passed, 0 failed, 17 skipped, identical to main at this PR's base (run 44271306222).
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: spell #1736's inline Nish programs as arrows
entries.body: The compact-class --explain-layout tests landed with 15 inline Nish function definitions while the corpus rewrite was in review; they are now const arrows like the rest of the harness's inline programs. IR is unchanged.
entries.author: Redis Stasa

entries.title: lay out a class pointer field in 4 bytes on wasm32
entries.body:
computeLayout gave every class pointer field an 8-byte slot, so on wasm32, where LLVM's p:32:32 lays a pointer out in 4, a class's size over-allocated and its offsets disagreed with the struct LLVM emits. A pointer-valued field (class, string, array, union, Result, CPtr) is now 4 bytes wide and 4 aligned on wasm32; native layouts and IR do not move. Debug info, field alignment and the string-join element loads read the same pointer width.

A new wasm32-layout section pins each test class's size, alignment and field offsets against what LLVM's wasm32 DataLayout folds for the emitted struct, and checks the allocation size per class. Moved wasm32 goldens are regenerated and declared in nish-cmp. A Result's own layout (resultLayout) still pads a pointer payload to 8 on wasm32 and is left open.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: spell the last host-importing inline programs as arrows
entries.body: The host-import section's entry programs import a host module but are not one, so they take the const-arrow spelling; the host modules keep `export function`, which src/host-module.ts reads. The allowlist reason for tests/parser/names-operator-calls.ts now names what blocks the codemod: functions named after operator words, not `catch`.
entries.author: Redis Stasa

entries.title: run the side jobs only when their inputs change, behind one gate
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: lay out an implements Compact class's links as 32-bit offsets
entries.body:
A class that implements `Compact` from the new `nish:compact` module now stores every field typed exactly as that class, or that class `| null`, as a 32-bit offset into the reserved arena range that stage 1 added. This applies in any class, across modules, and through interface and generic views. A field load decodes the offset and a field store encodes it. Linux uses a zero-based shape. macOS uses a based shape through `@nish_ref_base`.

A compact class is 4-aligned and allocated in 4-byte units, so a node of an `i32` and two links takes 12 bytes instead of 24. A compact class is never promoted to the stack. Every `align`/`dereferenceable` attribute reads the class's real alignment, including through an interface type. `--debug-info` describes a link as a 32-bit member. Its TBAA tag, debug type and pretty-printers are deferred to stage 2b.

The marker is refused with a diagnostic where C, Node or the layout rules would read the class:
- a header or N-API build (NL4021)
- a class exported to C or N-API (NL4020)
- a `declare class` (NL2795), or a field of a declare class (NL2796)
- a class holding a `Secret` (NL2797)
- a generic class (NL2798)

wasm32 builds, host page modules and ASAN builds compile the marker to today's IR. A program without the marker is unchanged byte for byte: nish-cmp shows no undeclared differences and declares none.

`Wide` is declared for stage 3, when the compiler picks compact classes itself.
metrics: bench/goose/tree.ts n = 24, 21 interleaved rounds, TNode implements Compact against the stage-0 prototype IR: peak RSS 385.5 MB vs 385.5 MB (0.0%), wall 1675.7 ms vs 1690.8 ms (-0.9%); against uncompressed ptr 0.50x RSS and 0.69x wall; noise band median 3.5% (ptr vs ptr-copy)
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: hold a CI lane's read set to what its commands read
entries.body:
scripts/ci-scope.mjs lets a side job skip when a pull request changes nothing
the job reads. Review of #1746 found three hand-listed read sets that missed a
file their job opens: cli.ts's fixtures for bootstrap, tests/self for
postgres-live, tests/runtime/range-test.c for fuzz-smoke. The 60-PR backtest
caught none of them, because it can only see lanes whose jobs failed in its
sample. The rule asks for the trace and a per-command test instead.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: report generic class instantiations in --explain-layout
entries.body:
Each instantiation of a generic class is now a candidate class for the
compact-class rule's five tests and gets its own --explain-layout line,
named as written in a type (TNode<i32>) at the generic class's
declaration, marked (std) when std declares it. Fields typed exactly the
instantiation or it | null count as links and holders, and new Box<T>(...)
records a made-site and constructor edge. Analysis only: no program's IR
changes.

entries.title: widen narrow C arguments and results with zeroext
entries.body:
A declare function with a u8, u16 or boolean parameter or return was emitted without zeroext at the declaration and at each call, so a clang-built C callee on x86-64 SysV or Apple arm64 read stale upper bits (toU8(511) arrived as 511). Every narrow (i1/i8/i16) foreign parameter and result now carries zeroext at both sites, including wasm --host calls.

Tests: tests/cases/ffi_narrow_zeroext
Fixes #1755
